extraction.name: FOMO60K
extraction.description: A large-scale, heterogeneous dataset of 60,529 brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans from 13,900 sessions and 11,187 subjects, aggregated from 16 publicly available sources. The dataset includes both clinical- and research-grade images, multiple MRI sequences, and a wide range of anatomical and pathological variability, including scans with large brain anomalies. Minimal preprocessing was applied to preserve the original image characteristics while reducing barriers to entry for new users. Accompanying code for self-supervised pretraining and finetuning is provided.
extraction.creator: Asbjørn Munk, Stefano Cerri, Jakob Ambsdorf, Julia Machnio, Sebastian Nørgaard Llambias, Vardan Nersesjan, Christian Hedeager Krag, Peirong Liu, Pablo Rocamora García, Mostafa Mehdipour Ghazi, Mikael Boesen, Michael Eriksen Benros, Juan Eugenio Iglesias, Mads Nielsen
extraction.citeAs: Munk, A., Cerri, S., Ambsdorf, J., Machnio, J., Llambias, S. N., Nersesjan, V., Krag, C. H., Liu, P., Rocamora García, P., Mehdipour Ghazi, M., Boesen, M., Benros, M. E., Iglesias, J. E., & Nielsen, M. (2025). A large-scale heterogeneous 3D magnetic resonance brain imaging dataset for self-supervised learning. arXiv:2506.14432v1.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Aggregated from 16 publicly available sources, including clinical- and research-grade images, multiple MRI sequences, and scans with large brain anomalies. Minimal preprocessing was applied to retain raw characteristics while improving usability.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 16 publicly available datasets, including MGH Wild, SOOP, BraTS-GEN, OASIS, MSD Braintumor, IXI, NIMH, DLBS, IDEAS, ARC, MBSR, UCLA, QTAB, NKI, and AOMIC ID1000.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: MRI preprocessing comprised three main steps: reorienting images to RAS (Right–Anterior–Superior) orientation, affine co-registration, and skull-stripping. For DWI scans, additional steps included extracting b=0 volumes and selecting representative volumes for b=1000 shell.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Minimal preprocessing was applied to preserve original image characteristics. Specific steps included: reorienting to RAS, affine co-registration, skull-stripping (using SynthSeg31), and handling DWI scans with b=0 extraction and representative volume selection. Skull-stripping was skipped if images were already defaced or skull-stripped by the dataset provider.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: No explicit annotation protocol described; dataset consists of raw MRI scans without labels. Accompanying code is provided for self-supervised pretraining and fine-tuning.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will continue to grow in future releases as additional cohorts and modalities become available. Versioning and maintenance are implied through the FOMO25 challenge and associated GitHub repository (https://github.com/fomo25/fomo60k-preprocessing).
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Brain MRI scans, which inherently contain sensitive personal health information.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aims to support the development and benchmarking of self-supervised learning methods in medical imaging at scale, potentially improving healthcare diagnostics and treatment through advanced AI techniques.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Heterogeneous dataset aggregated from multiple sources may introduce biases related to imaging protocols, patient populations, and pathological variability across datasets.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Dataset may have generalization limits due to heterogeneity in imaging protocols and pathological variability. Non-recommended uses include applications requiring labeled data or specific clinical diagnoses without additional validation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning for self-supervised learning methods in medical imaging. Usage guidelines include citing source datasets and using provided preprocessing scripts for reproducibility.
